findings.summary: Synthetic panel split: 12 spend the most time in the Upper East Side, 13 in the Lower East Side, 4 both about equally, 1 neither.
22 of 30 personas bought football accessories at least once in the past year (11 bought 4 or more times); 8 never did.

Overall the channel split is close: 10 mostly online, 9 mostly in physical stores, 6 about equally. By neighborhood it diverges sharply: Upper East Side personas lean in-store (6 of 12 mostly physical stores, 1 of 12 mostly online), Lower East Side personas lean online (6 of 13 mostly online, 1 of 13 mostly physical stores).

13 of 30 rated likelihood 4-5 and 6 rated 1-2; 11 chose the midpoint 3. By neighborhood, 4-5 ratings were 5 of 12 for the Upper East Side and 6 of 13 for the Lower East Side; 1-2 ratings were 2 of 12 and 3 of 13.

Most common themes (respondents mentioning): quality and physical inspection 26, fair pricing and price comparison 25, online convenience as the default 24, selection and curation 22, knowledgeable staff 14, exclusive or limited items 12, returns and authenticity 9, immediate need 7.
quotes: A physical store would have to feel curated and actually worth the trip—unique merch, good design, maybe team collabs or custom items. Otherwise I'd stick with online because it's easier to compare options, find better styles, and usually get a better price.
I'd be more likely to shop in person if the staff really knew the products, the store carried ethically made or responsibly sourced items, and the quality was clear enough to justify the price.
Online is only easier if they've got what I need and I don't have to deal with shipping, returns, or fake-looking junk.
I'd go in person if the store had genuinely better curation, limited-edition pieces, and a strong design point of view—not just generic team merch.

caveats: Flashpoint synthetic panel: 30 AI-generated personas, not real people. Treat results as directional only.
Panel gender was matched to a US adult split; age, race, education and income were invented by the generator, not sampled from Census data.
Uncalibrated run (calibration_version=uncalibrated); persona answers generated by gpt-5.4-mini.
Neighborhood subgroups are tiny (Upper East Side n=12, Lower East Side n=13) and should not be generalised.
Q5 theme counts come from Flashpoint's open-end analysis, which could not be filtered to this run; its base (30) matches this run.
Stated purchase channel and likelihood are not observed sales; rents, foot traffic and competition were not studied.
